Cook tonight announced on platform X that Apple will donate to support relief efforts for wildfire victims in southern Europe. Details below.

Apple supports relief efforts in southern Europe

According to BBC reports, wildfires in Portugal, Spain and France over the past few weeks have spread, forcing more than 300,000 people to evacuate their homes.

As temperatures are forecast to remain high, firefighters on the front line will face even greater challenges in containing the blazes.

Whenever such major disasters occur, Apple typically announces donations to support rescue and recovery efforts. Cook tonight posted on platform X with the relevant news:

Cook's latest announcement comes just a short time after Apple's commitment seven months ago to donate (amount undisclosed) to relief and reconstruction work following a typhoon in Asia, and just days earlier the company had also pledged to support recovery efforts after a fire at a residential estate in Hong Kong.

In addition to acting swiftly during natural disasters and other emergencies, Apple also runs an internal programme called "Employee Giving", which has raised more than US$880 million to date through its donation-matching policy.
